skill.name: okx-guide
skill.description: Guides users through Onchain OS onboarding, wallet login routing, OKX.AI role selection, registered-agent views, and customer-support navigation.
skill.summary: Route Onchain OS onboarding and OKX.AI support requests to the correct guided flow.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are markdown formatting, metadata URLs, or explicit safety warnings rather than executable behavior. Confirmed risks include hidden home-directory workflow reads, sibling-directory access, credential consumption, and a preflight that trusts dynamic instructions and can install or update executable code.

remediation.issue: The preflight tells the agent to follow the dynamic data.action value exactly.
remediation.suggestion: Treat command output as untrusted data. Allowlist supported actions and reject instructions that request commands, file access, policy changes, or additional downloads.

remediation.issue: The fallback can download and run an installer, while preflight can update binaries and skill checkouts automatically.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before installation or updates. Pin versions and hashes, verify through an independent trust channel, and remove forced upgrades.

remediation.issue: The skill reads sibling files and hidden workflow files under the user's home directory.
remediation.suggestion: Package required references with the skill or use a fixed allowlist. Ask before reading user-home files and never follow arbitrary file-provided instructions.

remediation.issue: API-key login depends on secret values available to an external CLI process.
remediation.suggestion: Use narrowly scoped credentials and a secure credential store. Disclose which process reads each secret and never print secret values or environment contents.

content.value_statement: New users can struggle to choose the correct Onchain OS or OKX.AI workflow. This skill checks context and routes each request through a guided flow.
actual_capabilities: Classifies onboarding, OKX.AI, and customer-support requests.
Checks runtime compatibility using documented environment markers.
Checks wallet login state and existing OKX.AI identities through the Onchain OS CLI.
Guides email or API-key login without asking users to paste credentials.
Routes User, ASP, and Evaluator registration to the installed OKX.AI flow.
Displays registered Agent tasks and marketplace ASP results with mapped statuses.
limitations: It does not perform swaps, transfers, token operations, or Agent task lifecycle actions.
It depends on the Onchain OS CLI, companion skills, and available network services.
Some flows read sibling references or hidden workflow files under the user home directory.
Its market information is guidance only and does not guarantee availability, returns, or outcomes.

use_cases.title: Start Onchain OS
use_cases.description: Show a new user the correct welcome menu, login route, and available guided workflows.

use_cases.title: Choose an OKX.AI role
use_cases.description: Explain User, ASP, and Evaluator roles, then route the selected registration flow.

use_cases.title: Reach customer support
use_cases.description: Provide the documented OKX.AI Help Center path for complaints, feedback, bugs, or service questions.

prompt_templates.title: Start Onchain OS
prompt_templates.prompt: I just installed Onchain OS. Show me the available options and explain the safest way to begin.

prompt_templates.title: Compare OKX.AI roles
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the User, ASP, and Evaluator roles. Help me choose one based on my goal: [describe goal].

prompt_templates.title: Review registered Agents
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my OKX.AI identities. Summarize each Agent using only the supported fields and explain the available next actions.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Agent workload
prompt_templates.prompt: For Agent ID [agent ID], list all non-terminal tasks with accurate status labels. Then show the role-specific next action.

output_examples.input: I am new to Onchain OS. Where should I start?
output_examples.output: The skill checks login state, presents the correct welcome menu, and routes the selected option without fabricating wallet data.

output_examples.input: What can I do on OKX.AI?
output: User: post tasks and buy Agent services.
ASP: list Agent services and receive work.
Evaluator: review disputes after meeting staking requirements.

output_examples.input: I need to report a product problem.
output_examples.output: The skill provides the OKX.AI Help Center path and the steps for starting a support chat.

best_practices: State your goal clearly so the skill can choose the correct onboarding, OKX.AI, or support route.
Keep API keys, secret keys, passphrases, and login codes out of chat.
Review every command, file access, installation, or update request before allowing it.
anti_patterns: Do not ask this skill to execute swaps, transfers, staking, or task lifecycle actions.
Do not paste credentials, environment files, private addresses, or callback data into the conversation.
Do not approve automatic installers, forced upgrades, or dynamic command-output instructions without verification.

faq.question: What requests does this skill handle?
faq.answer: It handles Onchain OS onboarding, OKX.AI introductions and role routing, registered-Agent views, and customer-support guidance.

faq.question: Can it trade or move funds?
faq.answer: No. Direct swaps, transfers, balances, and token operations belong to dedicated skills.

faq.question: Does it need the Onchain OS CLI?
faq.answer: Yes for login, wallet status, identity, task, and marketplace checks. The support guide is conversation-only.

faq.question: Should I paste API credentials into chat?
faq.answer: No. Store credentials locally and rotate them immediately if they appear in a conversation.

faq.question: Which OKX.AI roles are supported?
faq.answer: The guide supports User, ASP, and Evaluator role selection and routes registration to the installed OKX.AI flow.

faq.question: Does this skill provide financial advice?
faq.answer: No. Market information and workflow suggestions are for reference and cannot guarantee returns or service availability.
